text: This is the final third of the nightly pipeline: Load. Clean, resolved rows sitting in staging get written into fact_sales -- but only yesterday's new transactions, never the whole history, and safely enough to re-run if tonight needs a retry.

First, we close the loop on dim_product's Type Two history. A price change doesn't overwrite the row -- it expires the old version and inserts a new one with a new surrogate key, so historical sales still point at the price that was true the day they happened.

Then idempotency: before inserting, the package deletes any existing fact_sales rows for the date being loaded, scoped to that one day only, and re-inserts. Run tonight's load twice by accident, and you get the exact same result both times -- never doubled sales.

Three things make this load correct: expire-and-insert instead of overwrite, a delete scoped to a single date before every insert, and a row-count reconciliation between staging and the fact table before the run is ever allowed to log success.
All three packages -- Extract, Transform, Load -- now chain together under one SQL Server Agent job, scheduled for 1:15 a.m. every night, each step passing control to the next only on success.
The automated pipeline is live. Next, we build the first thing a Riverside employee actually opens every morning -- the store manager's report.
